strengths_deep_dive: The Hassan Foundation directs <cite id="3">88.2% of its total expenditures directly into humanitarian operations</cite>, which beats the standard 75% threshold for nonprofit financial efficiency [3]. Its focus on essential infrastructure like water wells and school reconstruction addresses acute basic needs in impoverished regions of Pakistan [5].
rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 2007, The Hassan Foundation is a faith-based organization operating primarily in Pakistan [5]. The charity focuses on humanitarian assistance, including <cite id="5">clean water projects and education support</cite> [5]. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $432,888</cite> [3]. The foundation directs <cite id="3">88.2% of its expenses to program services</cite>, exceeding the standard 75% industry benchmark [3]. However, its program ratio remains below the peer program ratio median of 88.9%. The organization accepts Zakat funds to serve eligible groups, specifically the poor and needy [5]. At the same time, operational data indicates substantial financial reserves, with <cite id="3">99.7 months of working capital</cite> held in reserve [3]. This accumulation creates a significant lag in deploying funds for immediate relief. Additionally, public data availability remains limited, leading to a low overall data confidence assessment.
